findings.reason: a worker reaching this clause either cuts the suite short and reports a subset as the whole, or exhausts its budget, and either way the section's gate proves nothing about the change.

findings.reason: a §2 worker cannot reach 0 s-to-10 s by shrinking the variadic input, so a correct implementation reports a failed gate, or the worker widens the change past the declared mechanism chasing a target the lever cannot deliver.
findings.text: done-when (2) demands "the point jet's cold compile falls to 10 s or less" from a mechanism whose lever covers 51.3 s of the 95.1 s wall (`variadic-op-splitter` 34.2 s plus `multi_output_fusion` 17.1 s, §5 line 73 and comment `c-20261027-compile-pass-profile-landed`), leaving an arithmetic floor near 43.8 s even if both passes vanished; the demand is also six times tighter than the 60 s clause this plan exists to meet (§0 line 47)

findings.reason: the decisions block is the plan's semantic authority, and a worker checking the ruling it is told to follow finds the opposite one.

findings.reason: a §3 worker completes the named redirect, counts the section met, and leaves a copy that still pays the copy's full cold compile, which is the cost this section exists to remove.
findings.text: §3 asserts "the expression is defined twice today" (the production `_row_program` and the copy at `scripts/prototypes/read_route/jets.py`), but `jax.jit(jax.vmap(_source_jets, in_axes=(0, None)))` is defined four times, including `scripts/prototypes/fixed_points/solve.py:121`, which the instruction "bound the owner ... and redirect the copy" leaves live, so the section's own goal ("one bounded program serves both") is not reached by the mechanism it states
